method: Tavily web search (mcp__claude_ai_Tavily__tavily_search) across government releases (war.gov, whitehouse.gov, exim.gov, trade.gov, ec.europa.eu, g7 documents), company press releases/SEC filings, and trade press (Argus, Fastmarkets, Reuters/CNBC syndications); key items confirmed with tavily_extract or with the publisher's own dated page. Each item carries the date of the action as stated by the source (YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM where only the month was reported). Amounts are as stated by the source; contract values are ceilings unless noted. Only actions by governments/industry in response to supply risk for gallium, germanium, antimony, graphite, rare earths/dysprosium/magnets and cobalt are included; scandium, nickel, tungsten and aluminium-only actions were left out.

items.summary: DoD awarded Graphite One (Alaska) a $37.5 million Defense Production Act Title III agreement, funded by the Inflation Reduction Act, to accelerate the feasibility study for its Graphite Creek graphite project.
Perpetua Resources was awarded an Ordnance Technology Initiative Agreement of up to $15.5 million to demonstrate a fully domestic antimony trisulfide supply chain from Stibnite ore for munitions.

EU negotiators reached a provisional agreement on the Critical Raw Materials Act, keeping 10% extraction and 40% processing benchmarks, raising recycling to 25%, and adding synthetic graphite as a strategic raw material for three years.
Treasury released proposed foreign-entity-of-concern rules under which EV tax-credit-eligible vehicles may not contain critical minerals extracted, processed or recycled by a FEOC from 2025.
Syrah started active anode material production at its 11,250 tpa Vidalia, Louisiana facility, which is backed by a US$102 million DOE loan committed in July 2022.
DoD conditionally awarded Perpetua Resources up to $34.6 million in additional DPA Title III funding for Stibnite construction readiness, bringing its DPA total to $59.4 million.
EXIM issued Perpetua Resources a non-binding letter of interest for up to $1.8 billion of debt financing for the Stibnite gold-antimony project.
DoD awarded 5N Plus $14.4 million to sustain and expand production of space-qualified germanium substrates in St. George, Utah, including germanium sourcing, recovery and refining.
The administration announced Section 301 tariff increases on Chinese goods, including 0% to 25% on natural graphite and permanent magnets in 2026 and on certain other critical minerals in 2024.
The Critical Raw Materials Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1252), adopted on 11 April 2024, entered into force.
USTR finalized 25% Section 301 tariffs on Chinese critical minerals effective 27 September 2024, with natural graphite and permanent magnets effective 1 January 2026.
DOE offered Novonix a conditional commitment for a loan of up to $754.8 million toward a synthetic graphite anode plant in Chattanooga, Tennessee.
A coalition of US anode producers (Anovion, Syrah, Novonix, Epsilon, SKI US) petitioned Commerce and the ITC for antidumping and countervailing duties on Chinese active anode material.
Syrah signed a binding offtake agreement with Lucid for active anode material from its Vidalia facility.

JOGMEC and Iwatani committed up to EUR 110 million in equity and shareholder loans to Carester's Caremag refinery in Lacq, France, with a long-term agreement to supply heavy rare earth oxides to Japan.

President Trump signed Executive Order 14241 directing expedited permitting for priority mineral projects and use of Defense Production Act and financing authorities to increase domestic mineral production.
The Commission adopted its first list of 47 EU Strategic Projects under the Critical Raw Materials Act, with an estimated EUR 22.5 billion total capital investment.
The administration initiated a Section 232 national-security investigation into imports of processed critical minerals and derivative products.
Ford idled its Chicago Assembly plant, which builds the Explorer, for one week after a supplier ran out of rare earth magnets under China's new export-licensing process.
Perpetua Resources was awarded up to $6.9 million in additional Army funding for antimony trisulfide testing, bringing total DoD awards to the company above $80 million.
CLEPA reported that several European supplier production lines and plants had shut down due to China's rare earth export restrictions, with about 25% of license applications approved.
Suzuki suspended production of its Swift car due to China's rare earth export curbs, Reuters reported on 5 June 2025.
The Commission designated 13 projects outside the EU as CRMA Strategic Projects, including the Songwe Hill rare earths project in Malawi.
IXM declared force majeure on cobalt supply contracts after the DRC extended its cobalt export ban by three months.
DoD agreed to buy $400 million of MP Materials preferred stock plus warrants and provide a $150 million loan, alongside a 10-year offtake of 100% of magnets from MP's planned 10X facility.

Under the same deal, DoD agreed to pay MP Materials the quarterly shortfall between $110/kg and the market price of NdPr for 10 years, taking 30% of upside above $110/kg once the 10X facility is at capacity.
Apple and MP Materials announced a $500 million agreement for MP to supply recycled rare earth magnets from Fort Worth, Texas, with shipments expected from 2027.
Commerce issued a preliminary 93.5% antidumping duty on Chinese anode-grade graphite, on top of preliminary countervailing duties set in May.
DLA issued a solicitation to buy up to 7,500 tonnes of alloy-grade cobalt over five years, worth up to $500 million, its first cobalt stockpile purchase effort since 1990.
DLA awarded United States Antimony Corp. a sole-source five-year IDIQ contract of up to $245 million for antimony metal ingots to replenish the National Defense Stockpile.
DLA cancelled its 7,500-tonne alloy-grade cobalt solicitation, citing unresolved statement-of-work issues, after six deadline extensions during a cobalt price rally.

Trump and Albanese signed a critical minerals framework, with each country to provide at least $1 billion over six months toward an $8.5 billion project pipeline including the Alcoa-Sojitz gallium project and Arafura's Nolans rare earths project.
Trump and Takaichi signed a non-binding framework to coordinate financing, trade measures and stockpiling for critical minerals and rare earths, and set up a joint Rapid Response Group.

The US announced China would suspend its 9 October 2025 rare earth controls and issue general licenses for rare earths, gallium, germanium, antimony and graphite, while the US cut fentanyl-related tariffs by 10 points from 10 November 2025.

items.actor: US DoD Office of Strategic Capital / Commerce
items.summary: OSC agreed a $620 million direct loan to Vulcan Elements for a 10,000-tonne magnet facility, plus $50 million of Commerce CHIPS equity and an $80 million OSC loan to ReElement Technologies.
The Department of War awarded ElementUSA $29.9 million to build a demonstration facility in Gramercy, Louisiana to recover gallium and scandium from industrial waste.

The Commission adopted the RESourceEU Action Plan, creating a Critical Raw Materials Centre in 2026 to coordinate stockpiling and joint purchasing, with buyer-supplier joint purchasing to start March 2026.
A $18.5 million DPA award to Lattice Materials for germanium crystal growth and a recycling line, approved 26 September 2025, was announced on 29 December 2025.
Atalco announced a $450 million partnership with the Department of War and Pinnacle Asset Management to sustain the only US alumina refinery and build a primary gallium circuit in Louisiana.
Trump issued a Section 232 proclamation on processed critical minerals that directed negotiation of supply agreements with trading partners rather than imposing immediate tariffs.
EXIM approved a loan of up to $10 billion, alongside about $2 billion of private capital, to create Project Vault, a public-private US Strategic Critical Minerals Reserve stored in US facilities.

items.actor: US State Dept / Vice President (Critical Minerals Ministerial)
items.summary: At a 54-country ministerial, Vice President Vance proposed a preferential trade zone for critical minerals with reference-price floors maintained by adjustable tariffs, and the US launched FORGE to succeed the Minerals Security Partnership.
Commerce issued final affirmative AD/CVD determinations on Chinese active anode material, keeping the 93.5% dumping rate and raising the main subsidy rate to 66.68%.

items.volume: 5,000 t/yr NdPr firm offtake + 50% of HRE oxide output
items.summary: JARE committed to buy 5,000 tpa of Lynas NdPr to 2038 at a $110/kg market-linked floor and the equivalent of 50% of Lynas heavy rare earth output, with Lynas paying JARE 30% of upside above $150/kg (capped at $10 million/yr).
The ITC made negative final injury determinations on Chinese active anode material, so the AD/CVD duties set by Commerce will not be imposed.
USA Rare Earth agreed to acquire Serra Verde, owner of Brazil's Pela Ema heavy rare earth mine with a 15-year US government-linked offtake, for about $2.8 billion in cash and shares.
DLA awarded Glencore a five-year cobalt supply contract worth up to $900 million in May 2026; the award was not competed and was reported publicly in November 2026.
The EU shortlisted tungsten, rare earths and gallium for its first coordinated critical-minerals stockpile and discussed storage with the Port of Rotterdam, Reuters reported.
EXIM's board approved a $2.9 billion, 13-year senior secured loan for Perpetua Resources' Stibnite gold-antimony project in Idaho.
G7 leaders at Evian committed to expand domestic stockpiling, share data on procurement and release mechanisms, and set up an IEA-supported joint cooperation mechanism for supply alerts.

items.volume: 100% of Phase I MREC for 15 years
items.summary: The Department of War committed $750 million to fund an offtake of mixed rare earth carbonate from Serra Verde's Pela Ema project, part of a $1.55 billion package including a $300 million DLA purchase commitment and price floors for magnet rare earths.
DoD made a $100 million follow-on preferred equity investment in Atalco, bringing its total invested capital in the alumina and gallium producer to $400 million.

items.actor: US DoW (IBAS) with Export Finance Australia, Japan, Sojitz
items.summary: The Department of War announced an estimated $174 million equity financing for a gallium plant at Alcoa's Wagerup refinery in Western Australia, in partnership with Export Finance Australia, Japan and Sojitz.

Glencore and Mercuria each committed $500 million as the first participants in VaultCo, which will use EXIM financing to buy and store critical minerals for US manufacturers; eligible minerals and purchase prices were not disclosed.
Treasury Secretary Bessent announced that the US–China trade truce, due to expire 10 November 2026, would be extended to 10 January 2027.
The Commission approved a second list of 46 EU Strategic Projects under the CRMA across 16 member states, including 10 cobalt, 4 graphite and 4 rare earth projects, bringing the total to 106.

China extended its suspension of the October 2025 rare earth controls to 10 January 2027, and the US extended 178 Section 301 tariff exclusions and postponed port fees on Chinese vessels to the same date.

Argus reported that DLA had awarded Atalco a contract of up to $350 million for 55.6 tonnes of gallium over a five-year ordering period, among $3.3 billion of IDIQ stockpile awards; the award date was not stated.

notes: Thin quarters: 2023Q3-2024Q1 and 2024Q3 have only 1-2 confirmed items each. Western responses to China's 2023 gallium/germanium/graphite licensing were mostly grants and rule-making, not stockpile buys. For 2024Q3, the antimony controls (effective 2024-09-15) met no confirmed government purchase in that quarter; the only confirmed action is the Section 301 finalization (exact day not confirmed, so month only). Japan's JOGMEC stockpile volumes are not disclosed; only its equity/offtake deals are included. No confirmed Project Vault deliveries or rare earth purchases as of the sources checked (Oct-Nov 2026). DLA IDIQ values are ceilings, not guaranteed purchases. 2026-11-11 is the Argus report date, not the award date. The 2026-02-11 Commerce graphite duties never took effect because the ITC voted no on 2026-03-12. EUR-denominated amounts (Caremag EUR 110m) are left as amountUSD null. Items on scandium (Sunrise OSC $400m, ElementUSA scandium part, DLA scandium), nickel and high-purity aluminium were left out as outside the six-mineral scope. Some URLs are syndications (Yahoo/stocktitan/prnewswire) of company press releases.
